CaptionOne thing I’ve noticed with almost every client who grew up with a mother wound or a chaotic home: They all have exceptional pattern recognition! Their brains were wired for survival in an unpredictable environment. It became a high-level scanner. They learned to read micro-expressions, shifts in energy, and the gap between what was said and what was actually felt. They studied the patterns so they could stay safe. But here’s the important part: As long as the nervous system is still stuck in hypervigilance, this ability stays mixed with fear. It can feel exhausting, overwhelming, or constantly “on.” When you heal the hypervigilance and the body starts to feel safer, something powerful happens: The same system that once scanned for danger now operates from clarity instead of survival. You gain cleaner, deeper access to one of the most powerful forms of intelligence there is: true pattern recognition. You’re no longer just reacting to threats. You’re reading life, relationships, and opportunities with precision and calm. That’s when it stops being a defence mechanism and becomes a real superpower you can use in your favour. Do you also have this kind of brain? 🧠 Comment below 👇 #innerchildwork #nervoussystemregulation

Caption⁨ وُلدت لالة فاطمة نسومر سنة 1830 بمنطقة القبائل، ونشأت في أسرة دينية وتلقت تعليمًا دينيًا جعلها تتمتع بمكانة روحية كبيرة بين السكان. ومع تصاعد الاحتلال الفرنسي، سخّرت نفوذها لتوحيد القبائل ورفع معنويات المقاومين، فأصبحت رمزًا للمقاومة الوطنية والإيمان بالحرية. برز دورها العسكري والسياسي بين عامي 1854 و1857، حيث قادت مع الشريف بوبغلة عدة معارك حققت فيها انتصارات بارزة، أشهرها معركة تاشكيرت. وقد اضطر الاحتلال الفرنسي إلى حشد نحو 45 ألف جندي بقيادة المارشال راندون لإخضاع منطقة القبائل، قبل أن تُؤسر سنة 1857 بعد مقاومة شرسة. توفيت لالة فاطمة نسومر سنة 1863 عن عمر 33 عامًا، لكنها بقيت واحدة من أعظم رموز المقاومة الجزائرية. وقد لقّبها الفرنسيون بـ “جان دارك جرجرة” تشبيهًا لها بالمقاتلة الفرنسية التي قادت الجيش الفرنسي ضد الإنجليز خلال حرب المئة عام، وذلك تقديرًا لشجاعتها وتأثيرها العسكري، بينما خلدها الجزائريون بوصفها رمزًا للقوة والإرادة والوحدة الوطنية. #dz #story #شخصيات #تاريخ #history⁩

CaptionWhat looks like a simple “lock hack” is actually a fascinating demonstration of how mechanical combination locks are engineered internally 🔐⚙️🧠 In this technique, a thin piece of paper or flexible plastic is carefully inserted beside the number dials of a suitcase lock to feel for tiny internal gaps or alignment points hidden inside the mechanism 📄🔍 As the dials rotate, small notches connected to the lock’s internal wheels shift position. By detecting where these gaps feel slightly different, a person can sometimes identify the correct alignment needed for the locking bar to disengage ⚡ Once all the hidden notches are lined up in the same direction, the user rotates every dial together one step at a time until the lock suddenly opens 🔄🔓 The reason this works comes down to the internal design of many low-cost mechanical combination locks. Inside the lock, each numbered wheel contains a small groove or gate cut into it. When the correct code is entered, all of these grooves align perfectly, allowing a locking bar or pin to slide into place and release the mechanism ⚙️📐 You can visualize the concept like this: Cheaper locks sometimes leave tiny manufacturing tolerances or gaps around these internal components. Those microscopic imperfections can accidentally leak mechanical feedback to the outside world 🧪🔍 That means: 👆 Slightly looser movement 📄 Different resistance 🕳️ Detectable notch positions can reveal clues about how the internal wheels are aligned. Security engineers call this a side-channel weakness — where information escapes through physical behavior rather than direct access to the code itself ⚠️ Higher-quality locks are specifically designed to reduce these vulnerabilities by using: 🛡️ Tighter tolerances 🔒 False gates ⚙️ Shielded wheel designs 📐 Improved anti-manipulation systems The viral popularity of videos like this comes from the satisfying moment where hidden mechanical logic suddenly becomes visible 🧠✨ Most people think of locks as mysterious sealed objects. CaptionFollow these 3 steps after buying your app domain. Basically split your app domain from your main domain. This makes working with different teams much easier. You should be using something like resend to make sure this doesn’t happen in the first place, but even they recommend setting it up like this. Despite his sincerity, every contract he takes ends in trouble due to corruption, leaving him frustrated and hopeless. Their relationship had ended bitterly years ago, and Gehna initially holds a grudge against Sachin, making his professional life even more difficult. As the story unfolds, Sachin uncovers a massive corruption racket involving politicians, contractors, and government officials who built an unsafe bridge using poor-quality materials. The bridge collapses, killing innocent people, but the powerful culprits hide the truth by blaming an innocent man and silencing anyone who tries to expose them. The film gradually shifts from light-hearted comedy to a serious political drama as Sachin loses loved ones and realizes the extent of the corruption around him. With the help of Gehna and an activist named Azad, he gathers evidence against the corrupt leaders. Despite threats, murders, and betrayals, Sachin refuses to give up. In the climax, Sachin finally retrieves the evidence exposing the entire scam. The main villain dies while trying to escape, and the corrupt contractors and politicians are arrested. Although his own family initially blames him for exposing them, Sachin ultimately earns respect for choosing honesty over money and proving that truth can prevail against corruption. CaptionThis video feels like someone compressed an entire season of chaos into one nonstop montage. Every clip throws people into sudden collisions, blindfolded games, fake horror-movie setups, and perfectly timed slapstick disasters that escalate faster than your brain can process what’s happening. What makes it so addictive is the contrast between normal everyday settings and the absolute madness unfolding inside them. One second everything looks calm… the next someone is flying across a room, dodging an object, or accidentally turning a harmless game into cinematic-level destruction. The editing style taps directly into the internet’s obsession with “chaotic energy” humor — fast pacing, unpredictable outcomes, exaggerated reactions, and zero time to mentally recover before the next disaster begins. Instead of one big punchline, the entire montage becomes a machine gun of nonstop physical comedy. That’s exactly why videos like this explode online. They combine shock, timing, and absurdity into a format that keeps viewers locked in from start to finish. Even while people question how some of the stunts were filmed safely, the sheer unpredictability of the clips makes them impossible to stop watching.

Caption🎬 This scene is from Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2. It features Professor Minerva McGonagall casting the Piertotum Locomotor spell to animate the stone statues of Hogwarts Castle, commanding them to defend the school against Voldemort’s forces. The incantation “Piertotum” is a clever play on the Latin word petra (stone) combined with totum (all), while “Locomotor” is used throughout the series to move objects. Together, they function to bring stone objects to life and mobilize them. McGonagall’s use of this powerful and complex charm is a display of her immense magical ability and her deep dedication to protecting the students and the castle she loves. It marks one of the most heroic moments in the battle of Hogwarts.

Caption🎬 The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey (2012) ⛰️🕯️⚔️ There are scenes you watch. And there are scenes you feel in your soul. For me… It’s this one. The laughter fades. The room falls silent. One voice begins to sing. “Far over the Misty Mountains cold…” And suddenly, what started as an evening in Bilbo Baggins’ cozy little home transforms into an ancient tale of a lost kingdom, a stolen homeland, and a people who have carried their grief for generations. Every time I hear Misty Mountains, I get chills. Directed by Peter Jackson and based on J.R.R. Tolkien’s beloved novel, The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey follows the reluctant Bilbo Baggins as he’s swept into an adventure alongside thirteen dwarves and the wizard Gandalf to help reclaim the Lonely Mountain from the dragon Smaug. Starring Martin Freeman, Richard Armitage, Ian McKellen, Ken Stott, James Nesbitt, Aidan Turner, Dean O’Gorman, Graham McTavish, and many more, the film beautifully captures Tolkien’s belief that even the smallest person can change the course of history. But before the battles… Before the dragons… Before the kings… There was this song. A song that carries centuries of loss, longing, and hope in just a few haunting verses. Richard Armitage’s quiet, commanding voice as Thorin turns a simple melody into a promise—a promise to reclaim Erebor, no matter the cost. It’s one of the most unforgettable introductions to a fantasy journey ever put on film. Some adventures begin with a sword. The greatest ones begin with a song. ⭐ IMDb: 7.8/10 📺 Available on Max, Prime Video, Apple TV, and Google TV (availability varies by country). #TheHobbit #AnUnexpectedJourney #MiddleEarth #PeterJackson #MovieRecommendation

CaptionAlexandre Desplat’s "Lily’s Theme" from Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 is a monumental masterclass in the neuroscience of tragic anticipation and melodic memory mapping. 🥀 While the early films in the franchise relied on the majestic, whimsical wonder of John Williams’ iconic theme, Desplat re-engineered the final chapters to mirror the heavy psychological reality of adulthood and sacrifice. From a sound psychology perspective, the arrangement works as an elegant emotional override; by stripping away the brass fanfare and complex symphonic decorations, the solitary, wordless vocal line targets our baseline mirror networks. 🧠 The brain doesn't just process this as background music; it decodes the vocal friction as a raw, human lament—simultaneously accessing themes of childhood nostalgia, profound isolation, and unspoken regret. It stands as an insightful reminder that the scores which anchor themselves within our cultural consciousness permanently are not those that attempt to blow us away with volume, but those with the rare maturity to let a whisper carry the weight of an empire. 🕯️ Some themes decorate a scene. This one completely shifts the gravity of your thoughts. ✨🏛️ #AlexandreDesplat #HarryPotter #LilysTheme #MusicPsychology #CinematicSymphony

CaptionKorean Toy Parents Can’t Stop Playing With A toy bought to entertain a child. But it’s 2 AM and the parents are still at the keyboard, pressing keys, watching it react. The kid went to bed hours ago. The adults are having too much fun. 😂 This is the secret superpower of great toy design: making something so satisfying that adults don’t want to put it down either. 🌟 The toy in this clip is a Korean interactive keyboard. It’s not complicated. A sound module, some LEDs, a responsive key matrix. But the combination of tactile feedback, immediate sound response, and visual reward creates a loop that hooks everyone regardless of age. We manufacture sound modules that go into products like this. The key factors are simple: latency under 10ms from key press to sound output, audio clarity that doesn’t distort at max volume, and enough current to drive bright LEDs without overheating the regulator. 🔥 A product that appeals to both kids AND parents is rare. It doubles the addressable audience without doubling the BOM. That’s the kind of design brief every factory hopes to get. So here’s my question: what’s the last toy you bought for a child that you secretly wanted for yourself? 🤔 #ToyDesign #MusicToys #OEM #SoundModule #ProductDevelopment #Korea #ChinaManufacturing #XDT #InteractiveToys #Parenting

Caption🎬 Interesting Fact: Dhurandhar is one of those films where the entry of a character is intentionally designed to leave a strong first impression on the audience. Filmmakers often spend a surprising amount of time planning these entry moments — from the background score to the camera angle — because they know the first appearance can define how viewers perceive the character for the rest of the movie. 🎥 Another Interesting Fact: Scenes like this are rarely filmed just once. Directors usually shoot multiple takes with different camera movements, lighting setups, and pacing so that editors can later choose the version that feels the most impactful on screen. 🤯 Interesting Fact: In many films, a scene that lasts only a few seconds for the audience can actually take hours to shoot on set. Lighting adjustments, camera setups, and performance timing all have to be perfect before the final shot makes it into the film. That’s why some entries in movies instantly feel iconic — they’re crafted to create a memorable moment the second the character appears on screen. #dhurandhar #bollywood #moviefacts #reelsviral #explorepage

Captionفي عام 1872، تم العثور على السفينة (ماري سيلست) وهي تبحر في وسط المحيط الأطلسي بكامل طاقتها، لكن الصدمة كانت عندما صعد المنقذون على متنها. السفينة كانت سليمة تماماً، والمؤونة تكفي لأشهر، وطاولة الطعام كانت معدة، بل إن فناجين القهوة كانت لا تزال دافئة! لكن لم يكن هناك روح واحدة على متنها. اختفى القبطان وزوجته وابنته وطاقمه وكأنهم تبخروا في الهواء. لم يكن هناك أثر لقتال، ولم تسرق الكنوز التي كانت تحملها. ما الذي يجبر عائلة كاملة وطاقماً محترفاً على ترك سفينة آمنة والقفز في المحيط دون سبب؟ وضعت نظريات كثيرة، من الوحوش البحرية إلى الاختطاف، لكن حتى يومنا هذا، تظل (ماري سيلست) أعظم لغز في تاريخ البحار. نحن نعرف كيف اختفوا، لكن لا أحد يعرف "لماذا".. ربما بعض الأسرار خُلقت لتبقى في قاع المحيط. 🌊⚓️ . . #قصص #غموض #تاريخ #اكسبلور #حقائق

Caption⁨ ⁨ عاش الأديب الروسي الشهير فيودور دوستوفيسكي جزء كبير من حياته في مدينة سانت بطرسبرغ حتى أصبحت المدينة مرتبطة باسمه وأعماله الأدبية ارتباطا وثيقاً فقد أقام فيها نحو ثلاثين عام متفرقة وكانت مسرحاً لمعظم رواياته الكبرى مثل الجريمة و العقاب و الاخوة كارامازوف وصل دوستويفسكي إلى سانت بطرسبورغ شابا للدراسة في مدرسة الهندسة العسكرية. وبعد تخرجه ترك الخدمة العسكرية ليتفرغ للأدب في هذه المدينة نشر أول أعماله الأدبية وبدأ يختلط بالأوساط الثقافية والفكرية. كانت سانت بطرسبورغ أكثر من مجرد مكان إقامة بالنسبة له فقد تحولت إلى شخصية حاضرة في رواياته أحياء الفقراء، الأزقة الضيقة، الشقق الصغيرة والتفاوت الاجتماعي الذي رآه في المدينة انعكس بوضوح في عالم رواية الجريمة والعقاب وغيرها من أعماله. بعد سنوات من السجن والنفي خارج المدينة عاد إليها واستقر فيها خلال العقد الأخير من حياته عاش مع زوجته آنا في شقة بحي كوزنيتشني وهناك كتب أجزاء مهمة من رواية الإخوة كارامازوف كما توفي في هذه الشقة عام 1881. باختصار لا يمكن فهم حياة دوستويفسكي أو رواياته الكبرى دون فهم سانت بطرسبورغ فقد شكلت المدينة خلفيةً لأفكاره وتجارب شخصياته وأصبحت جزءًا أساسيًا من إرثه الأدبي … #روايات #دوستويفسكي #روسيا #قراءة_ممتعة #اقرأ_الان⁩⁩

CaptionExiste um erro muito comum que faz milhares de trabalhadores perderem dinheiro todos os anos: acreditar que apenas quem fica totalmente incapacitado pode receber um benefício do INSS. No caso do auxílio-acidente, isso não é verdade. Se um acidente deixou uma sequela permanente que reduziu sua capacidade para o trabalho, mesmo que você tenha voltado à sua rotina normalmente, pode existir o direito ao benefício. O auxílio-acidente foi criado justamente para indenizar o trabalhador pelas consequências deixadas pelo acidente. E uma das maiores vantagens é que ele pode ser recebido junto com o salário, sem impedir o exercício da profissão. Outro ponto que poucas pessoas conhecem é que esse benefício pode continuar sendo pago até a aposentadoria. Ao longo dos anos, isso pode representar um valor significativo que muitos segurados deixam de receber simplesmente por desconhecerem seus direitos. Por isso, antes de concluir que você não tem direito, procure entender como funciona o auxílio-acidente. Uma análise correta do seu caso pode revelar um benefício que você nunca imaginou que pudesse receber. The track gained even more attention after being featured as the intense entry theme for Akshaye Khanna’s character in the Bollywood film Dhurandhar, introducing it to a wider international audience. Some songs become hits on streaming platforms—others leave a lasting impact on the big screen. “FA9LA” is one of those unforgettable tracks. Song: FA9LA Artist: Flipperachi Producer: DJ Outlaw

CaptionMichael Jackson danced to the instruments most people couldn’t hear. He would catch a subtle high-hat pattern or a baseline pop and accent it with a sharp kick or a wrist flick. Amapiano is a genre entirely intertwined with dance culture. It birthed global, viral dance steps because its slower tempo allows a dancer to exhibit incredible control, isolate body movements, and play with the space between the beats. Michael would have seen the footwork coming out of South Africa and immediately recognized a kindred spirit in the movement—using his signature precision to create an entirely new visual language for the genre. Ultimately, Amapiano represents the exact ethos Michael championed throughout his life: taking deep, traditional African rhythmic roots, fusing them with modern electronic innovation, and delivering a joyful, soulful sound that unites people globally on the dancefloor. He wouldn’t have just loved it; he would have mastered it. #michaeljackson #kingofpop #mj #80s #music

CaptionDocker Troubleshooting: Cracking Exit Code 137! Exit code 137 is a clear indicator that your Docker container did not shut down gracefully; instead, it was instantly terminated by a SIGKILL signal. In Linux, exit codes for killed processes are calculated by adding 128 to the signal number. Since SIGKILL is signal 9, the math equals exactly 137. This means an external force—like the Linux host kernel, a container orchestrator, or a manual command—stepped in to kill the container's primary process. The most common culprit behind this error is the Out of Memory (OOM) Killer. When a container exceeds its allocated RAM limit or the host faces severe memory pressure, the kernel terminates the process to prevent a total system crash. Other frequent causes include a docker stop command timing out after its default grace period, forcing Docker to escalate to a hard kill, or systems like Kubernetes evicting a resource-heavy pod. To diagnose the root cause, run docker inspect on the stopped container and check the OOMKilled field under State. If it is flagged as true, your application ran out of memory and needs its limits adjusted. If that field is false, scan your host-level kernel logs using dmesg or journalctl -k to see if an external system or manual command forced the shutdown. #Docker #DevOps #SRE #Troubleshooting #SysAdmin #Kubernetes #Linux #CloudComputing #Containerization #SoftwareEngineering #TechTips #Backend

CaptionSystem design has many terms that sound similar… …but they solve very different problems. Here’s the simplest breakdown worth saving: LATENCY How long does one request take? THROUGHPUT How many requests can the system process over time? BANDWIDTH How much data can move through the network at once? — REPLICATION Copies the same data across multiple machines. SHARDING Splits different parts of the data across multiple machines. — POLLING Keeps asking: “Has anything changed?” WEBHOOK Automatically sends a notification when something happens. — PROCESS An independent program with its own memory. THREAD A smaller execution unit that shares memory within a process. — LOAD BALANCER Distributes traffic across multiple servers. API GATEWAY Controls how clients access APIs. — CONCURRENCY Handles multiple tasks during the same period. PARALLELISM Executes multiple tasks at exactly the same time. — MONOLITH Built and deployed as one complete application. MICROSERVICES Split into smaller services that can be developed and deployed independently. Small differences. Big impact when designing production systems. Save this for your system design and AI engineering interviews. . . . CaptionAn artist spends hours building a highly detailed sculpture of Sauron, paying close attention to the armor, proportions, and cinematic detail. While adjusting the arm, something unexpected happens. The head suddenly shifts on its own. At first it looks like the statue moved by itself. But the real explanation comes down to physics. The weight inside the sculpture is distributed in a way that connects every part of the structure. When one section is moved, even just a little, it changes the balance of the whole piece. That shift can cause another part to move in response. It is a simple but interesting example of how structural balance works. In large or multi part sculptures, a small adjustment in one spot can send force through the joints and supports, creating movement somewhere else that looks sudden or strange, even though it is just physics doing its job. Caption🩸 Your period is about much more than just bleeding. During your menstrual cycle, hormonal changes affect your entire body, not just your uterus. As hormone levels rise and fall, they can trigger a wide range of physical and emotional symptoms. 🤕 Common symptoms include: 💥 Menstrual cramps 😴 Fatigue 🤯 Headaches 😣 Muscle and body aches 😢 Mood swings and emotional changes 🧬 Why does this happen? As the uterus sheds its lining, it releases compounds called prostaglandins, which help the uterus contract. These contractions can cause cramps and may also contribute to headaches, nausea, and digestive discomfort. At the same time, fluctuations in estrogen and progesterone can affect the brain, muscles, and energy levels, leading to mood changes, tiredness, and increased sensitivity to pain. ✨ For many people, these symptoms are mild. But for others, they can significantly affect daily life, work, school, sleep, and overall well-being. Understanding what’s happening inside your body is the first step toward managing it. 🧬 Follow for more amazing biology and medical science facts! @biologyexplicated

CaptionHomemade Coffee Creamer ⬇️ Recipe below, or comment CREAMER and I’ll send it over! Welcome back to Make It, Don’t Buy It. Where I teach you how to make everyday foods you usually grab at the store right at home. Today we’re making homemade coffee creamer. Like I always say, it’s not about making everything from scratch all the time. It’s about knowing how. Having the option matters. Some seasons you’ll make it weekly, some seasons you won’t, and that’s okay. Most store bought creamers are filled with gums, artificial flavors, and added sugars. When you make it at home, you control the ingredients and the sweetness, and you can customize it exactly to your taste. The best part is it takes under five minutes to make and can last you an entire week in the fridge. This is one of those simple staples that makes mornings feel a little more intentional without adding more work. Homemade Coffee Creamer Ingredients -1 ½ cups heavy cream (You can sub half for half and half, or do all half and half for a lighter version) -¼ cup maple syrup -1 tablespoon vanilla extract -Sprinkle of sea salt, optional Instructions Add all ingredients to a jar or container with a lid. Shake or stir until fully combined. Store in the fridge and give it a good shake before each use. Use about 2 to 3 tablespoons per cup of coffee, adjusting to taste. If you like it sweeter, add more maple syrup. If you prefer it less sweet, use less. Make It Your Own You can easily customize this by adding different extracts like peppermint, caramel, or hazelnut. You can also find more versions on my page including peppermint mocha, pumpkin spice, and sugar cookie creamers. CaptionEverything you see online is just a series of lightning-fast light pulses traveling through hair-thin glass. 🌐 The secret to fiber optics is a physics phenomenon called Total Internal Reflection (TIR). Inside the cable, a glass core is surrounded by a "cladding" material with a lower refractive index. When light hits the boundary between them at a shallow angle, it doesn't pass through; instead, it bounces back into the core with 100% efficiency. This allows data to travel thousands of miles even around corners without losing its signal. To turn this light into information, engineers use binary code. A pulse of light represents a 1, and the absence of light represents a 0. By flickering these lasers billions of times per second, we can transmit entire high-definition movies across the ocean in the blink of an eye. It is the ultimate fusion of optical physics and digital communication engineering. #engineering #physics #fiberoptics #telecommunications #techfacts

URL

CaptionThe Shadow (c.1909) By Edmund Blair Leighton At first glance, this painting looks like a beautiful medieval love story. A young woman stands beside the man she loves as he prepares to leave for war. The ships below are ready to sail, the evening light is fading, and for one quiet moment, the world feels still. But look closer at her hand. She isn’t touching him. She’s tracing his shadow on the wall. And suddenly the painting becomes devastating. Because she already knows something he refuses to say out loud: He may never come back. This painting was inspired by an ancient Greek legend about a girl so terrified of losing the man she loved that she traced the outline of his shadow before he left. Not his face. Not his body. Just the last thing the light could hold onto. That detail is what makes the painting unforgettable. A shadow isn’t real. You can’t keep it. You can’t stop it from disappearing. And yet she traces it anyway, desperately trying to preserve something that’s already beginning to fade. Even the setting matters. The castle walls, the waiting ships, the armor, the sea ..everything in the painting points toward separation. The future is already pulling him away from her before he’s even gone. Edmund Blair Leighton understood that the saddest goodbyes are often the quietest ones. Not the moment someone leaves. But the moment you realize you’re about to lose them. That’s why this painting still breaks people today. Because sometimes love becomes memory long before the person disappears. Follow for more famous paintings explained, hidden meanings in art, emotional masterpiece stories, and heartbreaking historical paintings posted daily.

CaptionWorking with multiple asynchronous tasks? Choosing the right Promise method can make your JavaScript code cleaner, faster, and more reliable. Here's a quick breakdown: ✅ Promise.all() Use when every promise must succeed. If one fails, the entire operation fails. ✅ Promise.allSettled() Waits for every promise to finish—whether it succeeds or fails. Great for independent tasks. ✅ Promise.race() Returns the first promise that settles (resolved or rejected). Perfect for timeouts and competing requests. ✅ Promise.any() Returns the first successfully resolved promise. Ignores rejected promises unless they all fail. Choosing the right method depends on your use case—not personal preference. Mastering these four Promise methods will help you write better asynchronous JavaScript, especially when working with APIs, dashboards, and real-world applications. Save this cheatsheet for future reference. Follow @codergallery for more JavaScript, React, and Frontend Development content. #javascript #reactjs #frontenddeveloper #webdevelopment #coding

CaptionMy name is Shahir and i work as a security engineer at amazon for last 4 years. I started with zero experience and now im sharing how i got here. Before entering college, I already had a basic understanding of cybersecurity and a clear goal — I wanted to become a pentester / red teamer. If you’re a beginner with zero experience, that’s okay. This is the path I followed — and it might work for you too. Comment “Roadmap” i will send you my free cybersecurity roadmap you ever need. 🎓 Year 1 — Foundations I focused on building strong cybersecurity fundamentals using whatever resources were available online. I studied interview questions, searched for answers manually (no ChatGPT back then), and spent time doing labs. Slow. Manual. But solid. 🎤 Year 2 — Teaching & Growth This is where things changed. I started giving technical talks and teaching others about cybersecurity. Eventually, I landed part-time teaching roles at technical institutes. I also started a small cybersecurity startup focused on workshops and talks. 📌 Teaching forced me to understand concepts deeply, not just memorize them. 🧪 Year 3 — Profile Building When COVID hit and the world slowed down, I went all in. I dedicated myself full-time to bug bounty and CTFs, stacking real achievements I could proudly add to my resume. 💼 Year 4 — The Struggle Phase This was the hardest part. While my classmates were getting placed, I was still applying. 2,000–3,000 job applications. No interviews. No responses. Still, I kept preparing — just in case. 🚀 2 Months Before Graduation Out of nowhere, I got an interview call from Amazon. I went in with an open mind and excitement. The interview felt more like a conversation . And then… I got the offer. 📌 Lessons: • Foundations matter • Rejections are part of the process • Consistency always wins If you’re in college with zero experience, don’t quit early. 👉 Follow for real cybersecurity stories 👉 Save this — you’ll need it later #cybersecurity #cybersecurityjobs #cybersecurityengineer #breakintotech #motivation kerala kochi malayalam jobs ktu barcelona spaiN

CaptionTrigonometry may look complicated at first, but it’s built on a surprisingly simple idea: patterns that repeat forever. The sine, cosine, and tangent functions all follow predictable cycles as angles increase. Sine and cosine repeat every 360°, creating smooth wave-like curves, while tangent repeats every 180° and includes points where its value becomes undefined. These repeating mathematical patterns make trigonometry incredibly powerful. They help engineers design bridges, allow physicists to study waves and motion, and even make GPS, satellites, and computer graphics possible. Once you understand the pattern, trigonometry becomes far easier to visualize—and much easier to solve. Follow @Meutrux for more technology and engineering. Captionif you have no projects on your resume start here 1. Project Ideas and Resources This repo is basically a huge list of project ideas for practicing your coding skills. It’s useful if you’re stuck in the “I want to build something but have no idea what” phase and want beginner-friendly inspiration across different types of apps. 2. Build Your Own XThis one is for learning how real tools work by rebuilding them from scratch. It has step-by-step guides for making things like your own database, operating system, Git, Docker, text editor, neural network, and more - aka perfect if you want deeper CS projects that actually teach you how things work under the hood. 3. App IdeasThis repo gives you app ideas organized by difficulty, so you can pick something that matches your current skill level. I like this one because it doesn’t just throw random project names at you - a lot of the ideas include requirements, user stories, and bonus features, which makes it easier to actually finish and turn into a portfolio project. if you want the links comment “project” and ill dm you! follow part 2 :) and save this so you can actually put projects on ur resume! #codingprojects #codingproject #computerscience
